sections.heading: The 16 Mahajanapadas & the rise of Magadha

blocks.text: By the **6th century BCE**, the Ganga plains held **16 Mahajanapadas (great states)** — listed in the Buddhist **Anguttara Nikaya** — a mix of **monarchies and republics (gana-sanghas)**. Among them **Magadha** rose supreme through geography, resources and ambitious dynasties (Haryanka, Shishunaga, Nanda).

rows: Listed in **Anguttara Nikaya**; e.g. **Magadha, Kosala, Vatsa, Avanti** (the 4 most powerful), Vajji, Malla, Kuru, Panchala, Gandhara, Kamboja.
**Vajji (Lichchhavi) confederacy, Malla, Shakya (Buddha), Koliya** — oligarchic assemblies.
**Bimbisara** (matrimonial alliances, first to annex Anga), **Ajatashatru** (defeated Vajji using rathamusala & mahashilakantaka), **Udayin** (founded Pataliputra).
Destroyed Avanti; capital shifted to Vaishali.
**Mahapadma Nanda** ('first empire-builder'); **Dhana Nanda** (contemporary of Alexander), overthrown by Chandragupta Maurya.

items: **Geography**: fertile Ganga plains, protected capitals (Rajgir's hills, then Pataliputra's river-forts).
**Resources**: **iron mines (near Rajgir), timber & elephants** for a strong army.
**Ambitious rulers**: Bimbisara, Ajatashatru, the Nandas built a standing army & centralised power.

blocks.text: By **c. 600 BCE** the tribal janapadas consolidated into **16 Mahajanapadas** (listed in the Buddhist **Anguttara Nikaya** & Jain **Bhagavati Sutra**) — the era of the **second urbanisation** (first since the Harappans), driven by **iron tools, surplus agriculture, NBPW pottery and punch-marked coins**.

items: **Two polity types**: **monarchies** (Magadha, Kosala, Vatsa, Avanti) & **gana-sanghas/republics** (Vajji, Malla, Shakya, Koliya) — oligarchic assemblies of kshatriya clans.

Others: **Kuru** (Indraprastha/Hastinapur), **Panchala** (Ahichhatra/Kampilya), **Matsya** (Viratnagar), **Surasena** (Mathura), **Chedi** (Shuktimati), **Assaka/Ashmaka** (Potali — the only southern one, on Godavari).

blocks.text: **Jainism**, systematised by **Mahavira (the 24th and last Tirthankara)**, teaches **liberation through the Three Jewels and rigorous non-violence (ahimsa)**. It rejected Vedic ritual and the caste hierarchy, later splitting into **Digambara and Svetambara** sects.

rows: b. **Kundagrama (Vaishali)**, 540 BCE; Kshatriya (Jnatrika clan); attained **Kaivalya** at 42; died at **Pavapuri**.
**Right faith, Right knowledge, Right conduct** — path to liberation.

items: **24 Tirthankaras** ('ford-makers'): 1st **Rishabhanatha/Adinath** (bull emblem; mentioned in Rigveda & as an avatar); 23rd **Parshvanatha** (Varanasi prince, ~8th c BCE, 4 vows — historical); 24th **Vardhamana Mahavira** (599–527 BCE).

**Mahavira**: born **Kundagrama (Vaishali)** to Siddhartha & Trishala (Jnatrika kshatriya clan); wife Yashoda; attained **Kaivalya** at 42 on the Rijupalika river; titles **Jina, Mahavira, Nigantha**; died at **Pavapuri (527 BCE)**.
**Five vows (Pancha Mahavrata)**: **Ahimsa, Satya, Asteya (non-stealing), Aparigraha (non-possession)** + Mahavira added **Brahmacharya (celibacy)** to Parshva's four.

**Triratna (3 jewels)** to moksha: **Right Faith, Right Knowledge, Right Conduct**; philosophy of **Anekantavada (many-sidedness)** & **Syadvada (may-be)**; belief in **Atman (soul)** & **extreme non-violence**; rejects Vedas, permits **Sallekhana (ritual fasting to death)**.
**Sects**: **Svetambara** (white-clad; Sthulabhadra) vs **Digambara** (sky-clad/naked; Bhadrabahu) — split over a **famine → Bhadrabahu migrated south with Chandragupta Maurya to Shravanabelagola**.
**Councils**: 1st **Pataliputra** (c. 300 BCE, Sthulabhadra — compiled 12 Angas); 2nd **Vallabhi** (c. 512 CE, Devardhi — final canon in **Ardhamagadhi Prakrit**).

**Spread & art**: patronised in Karnataka (Gangas, Rashtrakutas — **Gomateshwara/Bahubali statue, Shravanabelagola**), Gujarat (Dilwara temples, Mt Abu), Kalinga (Kharavela — Hathigumpha, Udayagiri caves).
Mahavira = 24th Tirthankara; Triratna; 5 vows (4 of Parshva + Brahmacharya); Digambara vs Svetambara.
Anekantavada & Syadvada (many-sidedness of truth) are favourite MCQ concepts.

blocks.text: **Buddhism**, founded by **Gautama Buddha**, offers liberation (nirvana) from suffering via the **Four Noble Truths and the Eightfold Middle Path**. Spread by royal patronage (Ashoka, Kanishka), it evolved through **four councils** into **Hinayana, Mahayana and Vajrayana** schools and became a world religion.

rows: **Birth-Lotus/Bull (Lumbini), Enlightenment-Bodhi tree (Bodh Gaya), First Sermon-Wheel (Sarnath), Nirvana-Horse, Death/Mahaparinirvana-Stupa (Kushinagar)**.
Suffering exists; has a cause (desire/tanha); can cease; the path (Eightfold) ends it.
Right view, intention, speech, action, livelihood, effort, mindfulness, concentration ('**Middle Path**').

items: **Four Councils**: Rajgir (Ajatashatru) → Vaishali → Pataliputra (**Ashoka**, 3rd) → Kashmir (**Kanishka**, 4th — Mahayana/Hinayana split).
**Middle Path**, Four Noble Truths, Eightfold Path; Tripitaka in **Pali**.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: Buddhism (life, doctrine, spread)

items: **Gautama Buddha (Siddhartha, 563–483 BCE)**: born **Lumbini** (Nepal) to Shuddhodana & Mayadevi, **Shakya** clan, Kapilavastu; wife Yashodhara, son Rahula; the **Four Sights** (old man, sick man, corpse, ascetic) → **Great Renunciation (Mahabhinishkramana)** at 29; **Enlightenment (Nirvana)** at **Bodh Gaya** (Niranjana river, pipal) at 35; **first sermon (Dhammachakrapravartana)** at **Sarnath**; **Mahaparinirvana** at **Kushinagar** at 80.

**Doctrine**: **Four Noble Truths** (dukkha exists; cause = tanha/desire; cessation possible; **Eightfold Path** ends it); the **Middle Path**; **Anatta (no permanent soul)**, **Anicca (impermanence)**, **Pratityasamutpada (dependent origination)**, **karma & rebirth**, **nirvana** (not God-centred).
**Sangha**: monastic order (bhikkhus/bhikkhunis — women admitted at Ananda's request via Mahaprajapati Gautami); **Tri-Ratna**: **Buddha, Dhamma, Sangha**.

**Four Councils**: 1st **Rajgriha** (483 BCE, Mahakassapa, under Ajatashatru — Sutta & Vinaya compiled); 2nd **Vaishali** (383 BCE, Kalashoka — first schism); 3rd **Pataliputra** (250 BCE, Ashoka, **Moggaliputta Tissa** — Abhidhamma added, missions sent); 4th **Kashmir/Kundalvana** (~72 CE, **Kanishka, Vasumitra/Ashvaghosha** — Hinayana–Mahayana split; texts in **Sanskrit**).

**Schools**: **Hinayana/Theravada** (Pali canon, arhat ideal, Buddha as teacher — Sri Lanka, SE Asia); **Mahayana** (Sanskrit, **bodhisattva** ideal, Buddha as god, idol worship — China, Japan, Korea); **Vajrayana** (Tantric, mantras — Tibet).
**Literature (Tripitaka, Pali)**: **Sutta** (teachings/Jataka), **Vinaya** (monastic rules), **Abhidhamma** (philosophy); Milindapanha, Buddhacharita (Ashvaghosha).
5 great events + symbols and 4 councils (Rajgir-Vaishali-Pataliputra-Kashmir) are the highest-frequency MCQs.
4th council (Kanishka, Kashmir) = formal Hinayana/Mahayana split; Tripitakas in Pali.

**4th council** → split into **Hinayana & Mahayana**; Vajrayana (Tantric) later.

**Theravada** (Sri Lanka/SE Asia), **Mahayana** (China/Japan/Korea), **Vajrayana** (Tibet).

blocks.text: Magadha's climb from a Mahajanapada to India's first great power ran through the **Haryanka, Shishunaga and Nanda** dynasties. The **Nandas** built the first genuine north-Indian **empire with a vast standing army and efficient taxation**, setting the stage for the Mauryas.

rows: **Mahapadma Nanda** — 'Ekarat', 'Sarva-Kshatrantaka' (uprooter of Kshatriyas); huge army; **Dhana Nanda** — Alexander-era, overthrown by Chandragupta & Chanakya.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: Magadhan expansion & the Nandas

rows: Bimbisara (contemporary of Buddha) — matrimonial diplomacy, annexed Anga; **Ajatashatru** defeated Kosala & Vajji (used *rathamusala* & *mahashilakantaka* war-engines); **Udayin** founded **Pataliputra**.
Destroyed Avanti (Pradyotas); Kalashoka held the **2nd Buddhist Council** at Vaishali.

First **non-kshatriya (Shudra)** empire builder — 'Ekarat/Sarva-Kshatrantaka'; huge army; **Dhana Nanda** was overthrown by **Chandragupta Maurya + Chanakya**; Alexander's troops mutinied fearing the Nanda army (Gangaridai).

items: **Why Magadha rose**: fertile Ganga plains; **iron ore** (Rajgir/S. Bihar); river-fort capitals (Rajgir, Pataliputra); **war elephants**; control of Ganga trade; ambitious rulers.
Greek accounts call the Nanda realm **Gangaridai & Prasii** — its army deterred Alexander at the Beas (Hyphasis).
Sequence: Haryanka → Shishunaga → Nanda → Maurya. Mahapadma Nanda = first empire-builder.
Dhana Nanda's unpopularity + huge wealth enabled the Maurya takeover (Chanakya).

**Dhana Nanda** — last Nanda; contemporary of **Alexander**; possessed a vast army & treasury.
The Nandas are credited with a strong **standing army** and systematic **taxation**.
Greek sources call the Nanda ruler **'Agrammes/Xandrames'**.
**Chanakya (Kautilya)** & **Chandragupta Maurya** overthrew Dhana Nanda (c. 321 BCE).

blocks.text: India's north-west drew **Persian (Achaemenid)** and then **Macedonian (Alexander, 326 BCE)** invasions. Though militarily brief, they opened **Indo-Greek cultural contact, trade routes and administrative ideas**, and — by exposing the region's political fragmentation — indirectly spurred Mauryan unification.

rows: **Cyrus & Darius I** annexed the NW (Gandhara/Sindh) — a rich satrapy; introduced **Kharoshthi script, Aramaic, sigloi coins**; Persian influence on Mauryan art (Ashokan pillars).
Defeated **Porus at the Hydaspes (Jhelum)**; army mutinied at the **Beas**; retreated 325 BCE, died 323 BCE at Babylon.
**Indo-Greek relations, trade routes, Gandhara art seeds, Greek accounts (Arrian, Megasthenes later), and a political vacuum aiding the Mauryas**.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: Persian & Macedonian invasions

items: **Persian (Achaemenid)**: **Cyrus** & **Darius I** annexed the NW (Gandhara/Sindh) by ~518 BCE — India's richest **20th satrapy** (paid 360 talents of gold dust — Herodotus); brought **Kharoshthi** script (Aramaic-derived) & Persian coinage/administrative influence; **Xerxes** used Indian troops in Greece.

**Alexander (326 BCE)**: crossed the Indus; won the **Battle of the Hydaspes (Jhelum)** against **Porus (Purushottama)** — impressed, restored his kingdom; **Ambhi of Taxila** submitted; army **mutinied at the Beas (Hyphasis/Vipasha)** fearing the Nandas → Alexander turned back; died at Babylon 323 BCE.

**Effects**: opened **land & sea routes** (Indo-Greek trade); Greek accounts (Nearchus, Onesicritus, Megasthenes) date Indian history; **Hellenistic (Gandhara) art**; catalysed Maurya unification; **Indo-Greek** kingdoms later (Menander/Milinda; **Heliodorus pillar at Besnagar** — Garuda column to Vishnu).
Battle of Hydaspes (Jhelum) vs Porus; army turned back at the Beas — key facts.
Persian legacy: Kharoshthi script + Achaemenid influence on Ashokan pillars.

prelimsPointers: **Cyrus** and **Darius I** brought the NW under **Achaemenid Persia** (Gandhara satrapy).
**Kharoshthi script** (right-to-left) entered India via Persian contact.
**Alexander** defeated **Porus** at the **Battle of the Hydaspes (Jhelum), 326 BCE**.
Alexander's troops refused to advance beyond the **Beas (Hyphasis)** river.
Alexander died at **Babylon (323 BCE)**; Seleucus Nicator inherited the east.
Greek writers — **Arrian, Nearchus, Plutarch**; the invasion left **Greek settlements & Indo-Greek trade**.
The exposure of NW's disunity indirectly aided **Mauryan** unification.
**Darius I** made NW India the Achaemenid **20th satrapy** (richest); **Kharoshthi** script from Aramaic.
Alexander vs **Porus** at the **Hydaspes (Jhelum), 326 BCE**; **Ambhi** of Taxila allied with Alexander.
Alexander's army turned back at the **Beas (Hyphasis)**; he died at **Babylon (323 BCE)**.
**Heliodorus (Besnagar) pillar** — Indo-Greek envoy's Garuda column to Vishnu (Bhagavatism).
mainsAngles: Evaluate the impact of Alexander's invasion on ancient India.

blocks.text: The **Mauryan Empire (321–185 BCE)**, founded by **Chandragupta Maurya** with **Chanakya**, built India's first **centralised bureaucratic empire**. Its administration and economy are documented in **Kautilya's Arthashastra** and the Greek envoy **Megasthenes' Indica**.

rows: King aided by **Mantri Parishad**; **18 Tirthas (high officers)** incl. Samaharta (revenue), Sannidhata (treasury).
**4 provinces** under royal princes (**Kumaras**); capitals Taxila, Ujjain, Tosali, Suvarnagiri; capital **Pataliputra**.
Described a **6-committee municipal admin of Pataliputra** and a **7-caste society**.
**State control of agriculture, mines, trade**; **land revenue (Bhaga) ~1/6**; Sita lands (crown); standardised **Punch-marked coins**.
Council of Ministers advising the King
Head of Police and Law Enforcement

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: Mauryan administration & economy

items: **Founder**: **Chandragupta Maurya (321 BCE)** with **Kautilya (Chanakya/Vishnugupta)**; sources — **Arthashastra**, Megasthenes' **Indica**, Vishakhadatta's **Mudrarakshasa**, Ashokan **edicts**, Buddhist/Jain texts.

**Central govt**: king aided by **Mantriparishad**; the **18 Tirthas/Adhyakshas (superintendents)** ran departments (Sitadhyaksha-agriculture, Panyadhyaksha-trade, Akaradhyaksha-mines, Sulkadhyaksha-tolls, etc.); **Amatya, Senapati, Samaharta (revenue), Sannidhata (treasury)**.
**Provinces (4)**: **Taxila, Ujjain, Suvarnagiri, Tosali** — under royal princes (Kumaras/Aryaputras); districts under **Pradeshika, Rajukas, Yuktas**; village = **Gramika**.
**Pataliputra municipality** (Megasthenes): **6 committees of 5** (30 members) — industry, foreigners, births/deaths, trade, manufactured-goods inspection, sales tax.
**Espionage**: elaborate spy network — **Gudhapurushas** (secret agents), **Sansthana** (stationary) & **Sanchara** (wandering) spies; women spies (**Vishakanya**).

**Economy**: state-controlled; **land revenue (Bhaga) = 1/6 to 1/4**; **Sita** (crown-land income); irrigation (Pushyagupta's **Sudarshana Lake, Girnar**); state farms, mines, monopolies; **Punch-marked silver (karshapana/pana)** coins; guilds (shreni).
Arthashastra (Kautilya) + Indica (Megasthenes) are the two sources — know what each says.
6 committees for Pataliputra municipality, 4 provinces under Kumaras, spy system — recurring facts.

prelimsPointers: **Chandragupta Maurya** founded the empire (c. 321 BCE) with **Chanakya (Kautilya)**; defeated **Seleucus Nicator** (treaty + 500 elephants).
**Megasthenes** (Seleucus's envoy) wrote **'Indica'**; described a **7-caste** society & a **6-committee** Pataliputra municipality.
**Kautilya's Arthashastra** — treatise on statecraft/economy; **Saptanga theory** (7 elements of state).
Capital **Pataliputra**; 4 provinces under **Kumaras** (Taxila, Ujjain, Tosali, Suvarnagiri).
Land revenue **'Bhaga' ~1/6**; **Samaharta** (revenue), **Sannidhata** (treasury).
Currency — silver **Punch-Marked Coins ('Pana')**.
Chandragupta embraced **Jainism**, abdicated, and died at **Sravanabelagola** (with Bhadrabahu).
Four provinces: **Taxila, Ujjain, Suvarnagiri, Tosali**; **Samaharta** = revenue, **Sannidhata** = treasury.
**Saptanga** (7 limbs of state) & **Mandala** theory; Arthashastra found by **R. Shamasastry (1905)**.
Provinces (4): **Taxila, Ujjain (both N/W), Suvarnagiri (S), Tosali (E-Kalinga)**.
**Samaharta** = revenue collector-general; **Sannidhata** = treasurer; **Adhyakshas** = dept superintendents.
**Sudarshana Lake (Girnar)** built by **Pushyagupta** (Chandragupta's governor), repaired by Rudradaman & Skandagupta.
Pataliputra city board = **6 committees × 5 = 30** (per Megasthenes).
Megasthenes described **7 castes/classes** in Indica; land tax **1/6 (Bhaga)**.
Arthashastra rediscovered by **R. Shamasastry (1905)**; ~15 books, 180 chapters.
mainsAngles: Describe the administrative system of the Mauryan Empire as revealed by the Arthashastra and Indica.

blocks.text: **Ashoka (268–232 BCE)**, the greatest Maurya, transformed after the **Kalinga War (261 BCE)** to a policy of **Dhamma (moral law)** and non-violence. His **rock and pillar edicts** — the first decipherable royal proclamations — spread Buddhism across Asia and remain India's founding public morality.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: Ashoka — edicts, Dhamma, legacy

items: **Ashoka (268–232 BCE)**, 'Devanampiya Piyadasi'; the **Kalinga War (261 BCE, 8th regnal year)** — recorded only in **Major Rock Edict XIII** — turned him to **Dhamma** (Buddhism personally, but Dhamma = a secular ethical code).

**Edicts** (first deciphered by **James Prinsep, 1837**): **14 Major Rock Edicts**, **Minor Rock Edicts** (first to name 'Ashoka' — Maski, Gujarra), **7 Pillar Edicts**, cave inscriptions (**Barabar caves → Ajivikas**), **2 Kalinga (separate) edicts** (Dhauli, Jaugada).
**Scripts**: mostly **Brahmi** (Prakrit); **Kharoshthi** in the NW (Shahbazgarhi, Mansehra); **Greek & Aramaic** at **Kandahar** (bilingual).

**Content of Dhamma**: non-violence (ahimsa), tolerance/respect for all sects, obedience to elders, kindness to servants/animals, truthfulness, **prohibition of animal sacrifice/festivals**; enforced by **Dhamma Mahamatras** (officers of morality) & Rajukas.
**Welfare**: hospitals for men & animals, wells, rest-houses, roadside banyan/mango trees, medicinal herbs (MRE II); ended the royal hunt.
**Spread of Buddhism**: **3rd Council** at Pataliputra; missions to Sri Lanka (son **Mahinda** & daughter **Sanghamitra** — Bodhi sapling), Central Asia, SE Asia — made Buddhism a **world religion**.
**Ashokan pillars**: polished **Chunar sandstone**, monolithic; **Sarnath Lion Capital** = India's **national emblem**; the **Dharmachakra** = national flag; art shows Persian/Achaemenid influence.
Kalinga = Rock Edict XIII; Prinsep deciphered; 'Devanampiya Piyadassi'; Sarnath capital = national emblem.
Dhamma is ethical, not a new religion — a common MCQ distinction.
